newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo invites UK businessmen to invest, cooperate.
newsitem.headline: Yugo invites UK businessmen to invest, cooperate.

text.p: Yugoslavia on Monday called on Britain to step up its investment efforts and become one of the nation's top five trading partners.

"Great Britain is not among top five Yugoslav trading partners and we invite you to find your place among the top five," Mihajlo Milojevic, head of the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce, told a business gathering.

Addressing a meeting of Yugoslav and British businessmen, Milojevic called on British companies to cooperate in trade, investment, banking and industrial production and to become co-owners or 100-percent owners in Yugoslav firms.

Yugoslavia's 1996 exports to Britain stood at $95 million and imports at $27 million. In January-May 1997, Yugoslavia exported $21.5 million worth of goods to Britain and imported $34.4 million worth.

Serbia and Montenegro were particularly keen to increase banking cooperation to revitalise its ailing financial sector and rebuild confidence in banks, lost in 1991 when the state froze individual hard currency savings worth more than $4 billion.

Foreigners can open free-trade zones, import tax-free goods for the zone or establish off-shore companies in Montenegro which pay a 2.5 percent profit tax. They enjoy tax-free imports of equipment and five-year tax holiday for new companies.
"We had an excellent kick-off meeting this morning with Deputy Prime Minister Nikola Sainovic who frankly laid down issues and problems ahead," said the head of the British mission, Robert Cardwell.
"The point I made was that this is a two-way process, we touched on the question of privatisation and issues of support and cash injection which is required."
